title: Certificate term/effective/expiry derive; expiry is month-end
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin (Settings Service), on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (behind the maintenance_reminders flag). These are numeric/date-accuracy cases (Rule 116): seed the exact inputs, read the produced value back, and compare it to the stated value - never eyeball, never accept "a number".
  2. A compliance service on an asset, ready to add a record ("+ Add record"). Compute each expected value by hand first.
custom_steps:
1. Enter effective month Oct 2026 and term 6 months; read the derived expiry.
  2. Enter effective month Mar 2026 and term 12 months; read the derived expiry date.
  3. Enter expiry month Feb 2027 and term 12 months; read the derived effective month.
  4. Type an expiry month that conflicts with the derived one and see which is kept.
  5. Enter a certificate whose effective month is months in the past and confirm the effective month is entered by hand.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Any two of term / effective month / expiry month give the third: effective Oct 2026 + 6 months -> expiry Apr 2027; effective Mar 2026 + 12 months -> expiry Mar 2027; expiry Feb 2027 + 12 months -> effective Feb 2026.
  • A certificate expires on the last day of its expiry month: Apr 2027 -> 30 Apr 2027; Mar 2027 -> 31 Mar 2027; Feb 2027 -> 28 Feb 2027.
  • A typed month wins over a derived one; a certificate that arrives months old has its effective date entered manually.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10565 (S8); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S8; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S8-R10: “Term, effective month and expiry month derive from one another: any two give the third. Certificate dates are months, never days, and a certificate always expires on the last day of its expiry month. A month a person typed always wins over a derived one”
  • S8-E2: “A certificate expires on the last day of its expiry month, not the last working day”
  • S8-E1: “A certificate arrives already months old, issued by another shop. The effective date is entered manually”
